content: Trachoma is an infectious disease of the eye and is recognized as the leading cause of preventable blindness worldwide. The disease is caused by the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis. It is transmitted through direct contact with secretions from the eyes, nose, or throat of infected individuals. Additionally, it can spread via contact with contaminated objects, such as towels or washcloths, that have been exposed to these secretions. During a physical examination, signs of trachoma may include scarring on the inner surface of the upper eyelid, redness of the sclera (the white part of the eye), and the formation of new blood vessels growing into the cornea. Treatment with antibiotics, such as erythromycin or doxycycline, can prevent long-term complications if administered early in the course of the infection. In some cases, surgical intervention on the eyelid may be necessary to address scarring and prevent further damage, which, if left untreated, could result in blindness. The global economic burden of trachoma is significant, with an estimated $2.9 billion in lost productivity annually. This disease affects approximately 84 million people with active infections and has left nearly 8 million individuals visually impaired.
